gaps.sentence: The consultant will ___ us on every stage of the merger.
gaps.explanation: 'Advise' is the verb; 'advice' is the noun.
'Lately' means recently and is typical with the present perfect; 'late' means behind time.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ midnight when we finally arrived.
gaps.explanation: 'Nearly' means almost; 'near' as a preposition needs a place object and cannot modify 'midnight'.

gaps.sentence: I was so ___ when I forgot her name in front of everyone.
gaps.hint: how you feel in an awkward social situation
gaps.explanation: 'Embarrassed' describes short-term discomfort in a social situation; 'ashamed' implies guilt about wrongdoing.

gaps.sentence: He gave a ___ summary of the 40-page report.
gaps.explanation: 'A brief summary' — adjective; 'briefly' is the adverb.

gaps.hint: noun meaning a moral rule; fixed phrase 'on principle'
gaps.explanation: 'On principle' means because of a moral belief; 'principal' means main or the head of a school.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ anything left in the fridge.
gaps.hint: adverb meaning almost not at all
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly' means almost not ('hardly anything'); 'hard' means with effort or solid.

gaps.sentence: The new tax law will ___ every small business in the region.
gaps.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb (to influence); 'effect' is normally the noun.
